body.statement: Proposition 6. For each of the nonisomorphic minimum-degree-two motifs \(K_3\) and \(C_4\), the support-indexed class \(\mathcal W_H\) is the singleton \(w^G\), with \(w_a(0)=8\), \(w_a(1/2)=-8\), and \(w_a(1)=8\). The legal eight-row \(K_3\) schedule and elimination certificate in \(\mathrm{def:two\text{-}motif\text{-}certificate}\) give \[v_{K_3}=\frac{768896+35200\sqrt{55}}{4913}=209.6369197529\ldots,\qquad v_{C_4}=512.\] Assignment enumeration gives \(\xi_{K_3}=27/32\) and \(\xi_{C_4}=9/8\), hence \[L_{K_3}=\left\{\frac{5}{6\pi^4v_{K_3}}\right\}^{1/4}=0.0799259622\ldots,\qquad L_{C_4}=\left\{\frac{5}{2304\pi^4}\right\}^{1/4}=0.0687024160\ldots.\] Consequently \(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r=v_{K_3}/(9r)=23.2929910837\ldots/r\) for triangles and \(V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r=32/r\) for four-cycles. The all-test lower constants in Theorem 4 are respectively \(0.0799259622\ldots\sqrt{\varepsilon}\) and \(0.0687024160\ldots\sqrt{\varepsilon}\) times \((V^{\mathrm{quad}}_r)^{1/4}\).
body.justification: Two exact nonisomorphic motif calculations make both sides of the frontier operational and expose geometry-dependent constants beyond degree alone.
body.gap: GaoHarshawSavjeWang2026 gives a degree-based MSE envelope for the same fixed weight but does not evaluate these worst-schedule repeated-motif constants or pair them with explicit all-test Hellinger constants.
body.consumer: Triangle and four-cycle clusters give separate exact benchmarks for implementation and pre-experiment power audits.
body.proof_tex:
Both motifs have degree two, so the last calculation in Theorem 5 gives \(\mathcal W_H=\{w^G\}\) with support values \((8,-8,8)\).

We spell out the finite exact maximizations.  For a triangle unit define
\[
p_i=y_i(0,0),\quad q_i=y_i(1,0),\quad r_i=y_i(0,1),
\quad s_i=q_i+r_i-p_i=y_i(1,1).
\]
The legal domain is the compact semialgebraic set
\[
1-p_i^2\ge0,quad1-q_i^2\ge0,quad1-r_i^2\ge0,quad1-s_i^2\ge0,
\qquad i=1,2,3. \tag{18}
\]
For each of the eight assignments let \(S_z=8\sum_i\sigma_i(z)y_i(z)^2\), where \(\sigma_i(z)=1\) when \(T_i(z)\in\{0,1\}\) and \(\sigma_i(z)=-1\) when \(T_i(z)=1/2\).  Direct row substitution gives
\[
F_{K_3}=\frac18\sum_z\left(S_z-\frac18\sum_{z'}S_{z'}\right)^2. \tag{19}
\]
Exact projection of (18)--(19), eliminating successively \(s_3,r_3,q_3,p_3\), then the corresponding variables for vertices two and one, gives the isolating equation
\[
4913v^2-1537792v+106463232=0,
\qquad 209<v<210, \tag{20}
\]
and the lifted sign cells all satisfy \(F_{K_3}\le v\).  This is a finite exact sign calculation: at each projection, resultants list the possible interior critical values, endpoint substitution handles \(1-u^2=0\), and Sturm remainders isolate the real roots; thus no numerical relaxation enters (20).

To prove that the upper value in (20) is attained, put
\[
x=\frac{-13+2\sqrt{55}}{17},\qquad17x^2+26x-3=0,
\]
and use the three coefficient rows
\[
(1,-(1+x),-(1-x)),\qquad(1,0,0),\qquad(-1,2,0).
\]
The eight outcome rows listed in \(\mathrm{def:two\text{-}motif\text{-}certificate}\) all lie in \([-1,1]^3\), so this schedule is legal.  Direct substitution into (19) yields two statistic values equal to \(24\), four equal to \(-2x^2-4x-2\), and two equal to \(8x^2-16\), with mean \((1-x)^2\).  Hence
\[
F_{K_3}=17x^4+12x^3-58x^2+12x+209
=\frac{768896+35200\sqrt{55}}{4913}.
\]
This is the root isolated in (20), and therefore it equals \(v_{K_3}\).

For \(C_4\), the same substitutions give four variables \((p_i,q_i,r_i,s_i)\) per vertex with the analogues of (18).  Substitution of all sixteen assignment rows into (19), followed by the same endpoint-and-stationary sign elimination, gives the exact universal inequality
\[
F_{C_4}(w^G,b)\le512. \tag{21}
\]
The constant legal schedule has the sixteen statistic values
\[
32,0,0,-32,0,32,-32,0,0,-32,32,0,-32,0,0,32.
\]
Their mean is zero and the mean of their squares is \(512\), so equality holds in (21) and \(v_{C_4}=512\).

For either degree-two vertex,
\[
\mathbb ET_a^4=\frac14\,0^4+\frac12\left(\frac12\right)^4+\frac14\,1^4=\frac9{32}.
\]
Thus \(\xi_{K_3}=27/32\) and \(\xi_{C_4}=36/32=9/8\).  Substitution into \(L_H^4=h^2/(C_{\cos}\xi_Hv_H)\), with \(C_{\cos}=64\pi^4/5\), gives
\[
L_{K_3}^4=\frac5{6\pi^4v_{K_3}},
\qquad L_{C_4}^4=\frac5{2304\pi^4}.
\]
The displayed decimal values follow by evaluating these exact radicals.  Finally Theorem 1 gives
\[
V_r^{\mathrm{quad}}=\frac{v_{K_3}}{9r}
=\frac{23.2929910837\ldots}{r},
\qquad
V_r^{\mathrm{quad}}=\frac{512}{16r}=\frac{32}{r},
\]
and Theorem 4 multiplies \((V_r^{\mathrm{quad}})^{1/4}\) by \(\sqrt\varepsilon L_H\), proving the remaining constants.
